questions.q: What is the key difference between a 15-character and an 18-character Salesforce Id?
options: They identify two different records
The 18-character Id is only valid on custom objects
The 15-character Id is case-sensitive; the 18-character Id is case-insensitive because its last 3 characters encode the capitalization
The 15-character Id is encrypted and the 18-character Id is not
questions.explain: Both forms refer to the same record; the 3-character suffix on the 18-character form encodes the case of the first 15 characters.

questions.q: What do the first three characters of a Salesforce Id represent?
options: The object's key prefix, for example 001 for Account
The year the record was created
The user who created the record
A checksum of the record's field values
questions.explain: The first three characters are the key prefix identifying the object type; 001 is Account.

questions.q: Why can 15-character Ids cause wrong results in an Excel VLOOKUP?
options: Excel cannot read text longer than 15 characters
VLOOKUP converts Ids into dates
Excel rejects any Id beginning with 001
Excel ignores case, so two Ids differing only in capitalization can be treated as equal
questions.explain: 15-character Ids are case-sensitive, but Excel's lookup is not, so different records can collide.

questions.q: How can you get the 18-character version of a record's Id inside Salesforce?
options: Add three random characters to the end
Use a formula field with the CASESAFEID function
Convert the Id to lowercase
It is impossible; only the API can produce 18-character Ids
questions.explain: CASESAFEID(Id) returns the 18-character, case-insensitive Id in a formula field.

questions.q: Which statement about loading data with Data Loader is correct?
options: Only 15-character Ids can be used in an update file
Only 18-character Ids can be used, and 15-character Ids always fail
Data Loader and the API accept either the 15-character or 18-character form of an Id
Ids cannot be included in load files at all
questions.explain: Salesforce accepts both forms on input, but 18-character Ids are the safer choice while you are preparing data in a spreadsheet.
